name: The Clockwork Tower
lesson: Finding persistence: scheduled tasks and registry Run keys, and comparing autostarts against a known-good baseline.
pivot_tip: Pivot on author and path. Real Microsoft tasks are authored by Microsoft; real OneDrive lives in AppData\Local.
reaction: updchk.exe re-registered itself under a new name. VELVET LOCUST is hardening its foothold.

e301.title: Autoruns snapshot: WS-FIN-0142
e301.tip: Unsigned entries in user-writable paths, named to look like something trusted, are prime suspects.

e302.title: Task XML: \HalcyonUpdateCheck
lines: Security log 4698: A scheduled task was created. Creator: HALCYON\m.okafor
e302.tip: A finance user authoring a SYSTEM task that runs from ProgramData at every logon is not normal IT.

e303.title: Run key export: OneDriveSync
e303.tip: Masquerading: the name imitates OneDrive, but the path and the process that wrote it give it away.

e304.title: Approved autostart baseline
lines: Policy: regular users are NOT local administrators. (Exception list: m.okafor - legacy)
e304.tip: Baselines turn 'looks odd' into 'is not approved'. Note the exception: Mira is a local admin, so the malware could create SYSTEM tasks.

rows.trigger: At log on of any user
rows.author: HALCYON\m.okafor

objectives.title: Snapshot the autostarts
objectives.desc: Investigate WS-FIN-0142 for its autoruns snapshot.
hints: Mira's workstation again.
Press E at WS-FIN-0142.
Open 'Autoruns snapshot: WS-FIN-0142'.

objectives.title: Find the rogue scheduled task
objectives.desc: Hunt the task table for a task on WS-FIN-0142 that wasn't authored by Microsoft or IT.
objectives.solution: search task where host="WS-FIN-0142" and author~"m.okafor"
objectives.success: \HalcyonUpdateCheck: authored by a finance user, runs as SYSTEM at logon.
hints: Searching for ProgramData also finds Defender's legitimate tasks. Try the author field.
Who authors tasks normally? Microsoft and HALCYON\svc_sccm. Who else shows up?
search task where host="WS-FIN-0142" and author~"m.okafor"

objectives.title: Find the rogue Run key
objectives.desc: Hunt the reg table for a Run key pointing into AppData\Roaming.
objectives.solution: search reg where key~"CurrentVersion\Run" and data~"Roaming"
objectives.success: OneDriveSync -> AppData\Roaming\odsync.exe. Real OneDrive lives in AppData\Local.
hints: Run keys live under CurrentVersion\Run in the key path.
Combine a key condition with a data condition using 'and'.
search reg where key~"CurrentVersion\Run" and data~"Roaming"

objectives.title: Gather the artifacts
objectives.desc: Collect the task XML, the Run key export, and the approved baseline.
hints: Three nodes: SCHED-SVC, REG-HIVE, GPO-01.
Press E at each one.
Open the task XML, the Run key export, and the baseline.

objectives.title: Spot the masquerade
objectives.prompt: What gives away the 'OneDriveSync' Run key as malicious?

options.feedback: Names are free to choose. Judge by path, signer, and who wrote it.

options.text: It imitates OneDrive but points to an unsigned binary in AppData\Roaming, written by updchk.exe, and isn't in the baseline

options.feedback: Most are legitimate: SecurityHealth and the real OneDrive are approved.
Time alone proves nothing. Lots of legitimate software installs during work hours.

objectives.success: Right: path, signer, writer, and baseline all disagree with the name.
hints: Compare against the baseline and the real OneDrive entry.
Where does real OneDrive live? Who wrote this key?
The answer mentions AppData\Roaming, unsigned, and updchk.exe.

objectives.title: Form a hypothesis
objectives.desc: Press B. Pin the proof and choose.
objectives.prompt: How is VELVET LOCUST surviving reboots on WS-FIN-0142?

options.text: Two persistence mechanisms: a SYSTEM scheduled task at logon and a per-user Run key masquerading as OneDrive

options.feedback: Check the service list later. Here the evidence is a task and a Run key.

options.text: It doesn't persist; a reboot would clean it
options.feedback: The task and Run key both relaunch it at logon.
Look at the registry export too. Adversaries often plant backups.

hints: Pin the task XML and the Run key export.
How many separate mechanisms did you find?
Pin e302 and e303, then choose the 'two persistence mechanisms' option.

objectives.title: Map it to ATT&CK
objectives.desc: Press M and map both findings. Think about what the adversary achieved.
hints: Both findings keep the adversary in place across reboots.
Persistence column.
f1 -> T1053.005 Scheduled Task; f2 -> T1547.001 Registry Run Keys (Persistence).

objectives.title: Respond
objectives.desc: Press R. Preserve, then remove persistence and fix the root cause.
hints: Export evidence before deleting it.
Remove both mechanisms and quarantine both binaries.
Export, delete task, remove Run value, quarantine binaries, remove local admin.

f1.text: A SYSTEM scheduled task relaunches updchk.exe at every logon
f1.hint: Which Windows feature runs programs on a trigger?

f2.text: A Run key named like OneDrive starts odsync.exe at user logon
f2.hint: It's an autostart entry in the registry.

responses.label: Export the task XML, Run key, and both binaries as evidence
responses.description: Preserve everything with hashes before changing the host.
responses.tradeoff: Takes a minute. You can't un-delete evidence.

responses.label: Delete the \HalcyonUpdateCheck task
responses.too_early: Export it first. Once deleted, the task XML and its timestamps are gone.

responses.label: Remove the OneDriveSync Run value
responses.description: Delete the masquerading Run key value.

responses.label: Quarantine updchk.exe and odsync.exe
responses.tradeoff: Removes the payloads the persistence launches.
responses.too_early: Copy the binaries into evidence first.

responses.label: Remove m.okafor from local Administrators
responses.description: Close the baseline exception that let the malware create SYSTEM tasks.
responses.tradeoff: Mira may need IT for some installs. Worth it.

responses.label: Delete every scheduled task on the host
responses.tradeoff: Breaks Windows maintenance and destroys evidence.
responses.feedback: Defender scans, updates, and inventory just broke, and the evidence went with them.

responses.label: Wait 24 hours to see what the task does
responses.tradeoff: VELVET LOCUST keeps moving while you watch.
responses.feedback: You already know what it does. Waiting just gave them time.
